===== FILE 4568__1.pdf =====
August 20, 2025
Dr. Steven L. Lieberman
Acting Under Secretary for Health
Department of Veterans Affairs
810 Vermont Avenue NW
Washington, DC 20420
Re: 38 CFR Part 17, RIN 2900-AS31
Concerned Women for America (CWA) is the largest public policy organization for 
women, championing Biblical values and constitutional principles in all levels of public 
policy. CWA is led by Penny Young Nance, proud mother of a Second Lieutenant in the 
United States Army. Our organization serves as a voice for countless veterans and 
military families among our 500,000 grassroots members. Teresa Pregnall, our Virginia 
state director and a member of our Board of Directors, is a veteran herself. CWA is 
explicitly pro-military and pro-life; we affirm national sovereignty, and we believe that 
pro-life is pro-woman in every circumstance. 
CWA strongly supports the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) proposed rule to 
reinstate the lawful exclusion of abortions and abortion counseling from the Civilian 
Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA) and VA 
medical benefits packages. 
In September of 2022, President Biden issued an Interim Final Rule (IFR) ordering the 
VA to include abortion and abortion counseling services among CHAMPVA and VA 
healthcare benefits. The IFR is a plain violation of longstanding federal law, and CWA 
firmly believes that the Biden-era order defies the will of hard-working American 
taxpayers while harming veterans and their families. 
CHAMPVA and VA healthcare benefits are federally funded programs; as such, they 
must operate in accordance with the rule of law and the will of the American people. 
The Veterans Health Care Act of 1992 (VHCA) stipulates that American taxpayer dollars 

may not fund abortions in any federal medical benefits program for veterans and their 
dependents. The VHCA was passed in 1992 to mirror the legacy of the 1976 Hyde 
Amendment, an annual rider in the Health and Human Services appropriations text that 
bars taxpayer dollars from being spent on abortions through Medicaid. 
After almost fifty years as law, the Hyde Amendment has saved an estimated 2.56 
million children from abortion and prevented coerced taxpayer funding of abortions.1 
Americans support the Hyde family of amendments, including the VHCA: sixty percent 
oppose or strongly oppose taxpayer funding of abortions.2 Most American taxpayers 
find the use of their money towards abortions morally objectionable. The illegal, coerced 
taxpayer funding of abortion in VA hospitals initiated under the Biden Administration is a 
grave violation of the American conscience and an abuse of hard-earned taxpayer 
dollars. 
CWA also rejects former President Biden’s claim that women “need” abortions. Abortion 
is an affront to womanhood. Pro-life is pro-woman, and as long as the VA provides 
abortions, it cannot offer quality care to female service members and veteran families. 
Pregnancy is a unique female capability worthy of unique support in our military—not 
violent termination. As a leading pro-life organization, CWA knows that abortion harms 
women. 
Studies have shown that women who undergo abortions are 81% more likely to 
experience adverse mental health conditions, including depression, anxiety, suicidal 
behavior, substance abuse, insomnia, nightmares, isolation/loneliness, and regret. 
According to the European Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology and Reproductive 
Biology, 60% of women report emotional distress after an abortion, and 30% of those 
experience “severe” distress. The Obstetrical and Gynecological Survey classifies 
abortion as a risk factor for self-harm and mood disorders. 
Some of the medical and physical risks of abortion include cervical damage, uterine 
scarring, future premature birth(s), future miscarriage(s), future ectopic pregnancies, 
heavy bleeding, sepsis, placenta previa, perforation of the uterus, and, in some cases, 
death.3 One abortion increases a woman’s risk of breast cancer by 44%.4
1 New, Michael J. (2023). “Hyde @ 40: Analyzing the Impact of the Hyde Amendment with July 2020 and 
2023 Addenda.” Charlotte Lozier Institute. Hyde @ 40: Analyzing the Impact of the Hyde Amendment with 
July 2020 and June 2023 Addenda - Lozier Institute
2 McCormack, John. (2023). “New Poll on Abortion: Most Americans Opposed Taxpayer Funding.” 
National Review. New Poll on Abortion: Most Americans Oppose Taxpayer Funding | National Review 
3 “Abortion Risks.” Students for Life of America. Abortion Risks - Students for Life of America
4 Huang, Y., Zhang, X., Li, W. et al. A meta-analysis of the association between induced abortion and 
breast cancer risk among Chinese females. Cancer Causes Control 25, 227–236 (2014). 
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10552-013-0325-7

Beyond harming women, abortion is never medically necessary—there is no medical 
condition that requires an induced abortion to save a woman’s life. There are legitimate, 
ethical, medical solutions to every life-threatening prenatal condition, such as pre-
eclampsia, hemorrhage, infection, and cardiovascular collapse. In the first trimester of 
pregnancy, maternal-fetal separation5 allows an unborn child (embryo or fetus) a 
dignified, painless death in a life-or-death scenario where a pregnancy must be ended 
to save a woman’s life. First-trimester maternal-fetal separation may result in the death 
of the premature child, but the separation is not an abortion. In the second trimester, 
early delivery is the ethical alternative to a painful dismemberment abortion and, paired 
with NICU treatment, allows the baby a chance to live while saving her mother’s life. In 
the third trimester, early delivery via induced labor or C-section is always safer, faster, 
and less expensive than a three-day late-term abortion (which includes induced cardiac 
arrest in the child, cervical dilation, and stillbirth).6 
Female servicemembers, veterans, and veteran family members deserve 
comprehensive, life-affirming, and life-saving pregnancy care in VA hospitals, and their 
unborn sons and daughters deserve the dignity befitting the children of 
servicemembers. Abortions are always cruel—never lifesaving, necessary, or beneficial. 
Life-affirming care, as described, delivers quality care while preserving human life and 
dignity for mothers and their unborn children. 
To be clear, life-affirming prenatal and postnatal treatment for veterans and CHAMPVA 
beneficiaries includes ectopic pregnancy care and miscarriage management. These 
treatments are explicitly not abortions7 and should be provided to women in need of 
these procedures at VA hospitals.
Abortion does not just harm women; it also ends the life of a human being. Ninety-six 
percent of biologists agree that human life begins at conception—the life of a military 
child, then, begins with fertilization. At VA hospitals, that means an abortion ends the life 
of a military child. VA doctors have an obligation to two patients in every pregnancy: the 
maternal patient and the fetal patient. 
Every unborn child possesses a unique genetic code and capacity for human 
development from conception, and his or her personhood is not limited by size, location, 
stage of development, or level of dependency. All human life bears the dignity due to 
5 “Premature Delivery is Not Induced Abortion.” American Association of Pro-life Obstetricians and 
Gynecologists. (2013). Premature Delivery is Not Induced Abortion | AAPLOG - American Association of 
Pro-life Obstetricians & Gynecologists
6 “Concluding Pregnancy Ethically.” American Association of Pro-life Obstetricians and Gynecologists. 
(2022). PG-10-Concluding-Pregnancy-Ethically-updated.pdf
7 “AAPLOG Statement: Clarification of Abortion Restrictions.” American Association of Pro-life 
Obstetricians and Gynecologists. (2022). AAPLOG Statement: Clarification of Abortion Restrictions | 
AAPLOG - American Association of Pro-life Obstetricians & Gynecologists

humans created in the Image of God and owed a constitutional right to life—boy or girl, 
abled or disabled, expected or unexpected. 
All in all, CWA affirms that abortion is not healthcare because pregnancy is never a 
disease or a disorder. Healthcare is broadly defined as “the field concerned with the 
maintenance or restoration of the health of the body or mind.” Abortion both intentionally 
ends a human life in utero and harms a woman's body and mind, and it is not 
“maintenance” or “restoration”; it is intentional killing.8 CWA is confident that the 
Veterans Administration exists to honor and extend the lives of United States veterans 
and their loved ones, not to illegally end lives via abortion on the taxpayers' dime. 
CWA regrets that the Biden administration lawlessly allowed federal funds to sponsor 
aborting thousands of unborn military sons and daughters. This illegal, undignified, anti-
woman, and un-American violation of the law must end. Abortion is not healthcare 
because pregnancy is not a disease, and the Department of Veterans Affairs must 
provide quality healthcare to women in uniform. CWA expects the VA to proceed in 
reinstating the full exclusion of abortions and abortion counseling from the VA and 
CHAMPVA medical benefits packages in accordance with the Veterans Health Care Act 
of 1992.
8 Skop, Ingrid. (2024). “Is Induced Abortion Healthcare?” Charlotte Lozier Institute.  Is Induced Abortion 
Health Care? - Lozier Institute
